items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: He said, "You play clarinet, huh?" I said, "Yeah, I try to." "How'd you like to make some records?" I said, "Fine."

ctx.x: It was just a record, two sides. Seventy-five cents. Yeah. Speaking about recording, the next session I did was with Mamie Smith and the way Peery Bradford heard me -- he was her manager then and also the writer of those tunes -- I lived at 130th Street and Peery lived directly behind me on 129th Street and he had heard me practicing on my house and he said, 'Hey, clarinet player,' I didn't know him, he didn't know

me. He said, "You play clarinet, huh?" I said, "Yeah, I try to." "How'd you like to make some records?" I said, "Fine." "Come on over my house," so I strapped my clarinet case on my back and climbed over the back fence and went through his kitchen upstairs and there was Mamie Smith sitting there.
That's when you met Mamie Smith.
